text:
Sam (support): Hey team — escalated from ACME. They started seeing p95/p99 latency regressions overnight on our hosted API for rw-13b when the quantization profile was flipped to `aggressive-int8-v2`. No errors, just slower tails. Sample request_id: req_0a9c3f. p95 jumped ~360ms -> ~950ms, p99 >2s. Can someone look? :eyes:

Alex (eng-runtime): Thanks — can you paste the deployment id, route, and example request payload? Also which rollout time did we push `aggressive-int8-v2`?

Sam (support): Deployment: dsp-hosted-13b-42, route `/v1/generate-rw13`. Rollout timestamp (canary -> 100%): 2026-03-14T03:10Z. Example minimal payload:

```json
{"model":"rw-13b","input":"Summarize: ...","max_tokens":128,"temperature":0.2}
```

Performance summary from monitoring (aggregated):
- BEFORE (balanced-int8-v1): p50=120ms, p95=360ms, p99=720ms
- AFTER (aggressive-int8-v2): p50=110ms, p95=950ms, p99=2400ms
Tokenization profile: avg input tokens 42, avg output 64.

Priya (eng-ml): Do we have quant calibration logs? Aggressive int8 often uses per-channel scales with asymmetric ranges — if calibration corpus isn't representative, you can get pathological kernel choices / dequant noise. Quick question: was `calibrate_samples=100` or higher?

Sam (support): Calibration job metadata (from deployment artifacts): `calibrate_samples=50`, `corpus=quickstart-snippets-v1`. I can re-run with more samples but customer wants immediate mitigation.

Alex (eng-runtime): Alright two likely paths: 1) some int8 kernels are faster but have strict memory alignment; if input shapes changed we may be hitting fallback codepaths that are slower (e.g., CPU fallback or slower matmul path). 2) Batching/queuing shift: aggressive quant sometimes reduces compute but increases memory traffic leading to longer GC/eviction stalls at high concurrency which blows up tails.

Here's a runtime trace snippet we pulled from the worker logs around the slow request (req_0a9c3f):

```
[2026-03-15T02:18:12.341Z] route=/v1/generate-rw13 req=req_0a9c3f selected_kernel=int8_matmul_fast
[2026-03-15T02:18:12.347Z] kernel_exec_start gpu0:block0
[2026-03-15T02:18:12.612Z] kernel_exec_end duration=265ms
[2026-03-15T02:18:12.613Z] fallback: matmul_reorder_slow_path (alignment mismatch)
[2026-03-15T02:18:13.900Z] kvcache_miss=true cache_miss_penalty=420ms
[2026-03-15T02:18:14.800Z] response_sent duration=2477ms
```

Note the `fallback` and `kvcache_miss` lines — that's suspicious.

Tara (eng-sre): If kv-cache misses spiked, that explains tails. We should check hit ratios and also running concurrency. Also apply temporary admission control so a few expensive requests don't queue everything.

Sam (support): Customer is on hosted (not dedicated). They want rollback if that's fastest. I can trigger rollback to `balanced-int8-v1` if agreed.

Alex (eng-runtime): I recommend a two-step mitigation: immediate fallback to fp16 for that deployment (fastest to change), and also roll back the quant profile across canary if we see improvement. Steps: 1) patch deployment to set `model_override.dtype=fp16` or set env `REDWOOD_MODEL_FORCE_FP16=1` then restart workers for that deployment (rolling restart). 2) if users need int8 for cost, schedule a controlled re-calibration with `calibrate_samples=1000` and `representative_corpus=prod_30days_top_prompts` before re-enabling aggressive-int8-v2.

Command to force fp16 via CLI (safe, immediate):

```
redwoodctl deploy update --id dsp-hosted-13b-42 --set model_override.dtype=fp16 --rolling-restart
```

Or via API patch: `PATCH /deployments/dsp-hosted-13b-42` body `{ "model_override": {"dtype":"fp16"}}`.

Priya (eng-ml): Also consider re-running the quantization pipeline with `--per_channel --clip_mode=relu` and `--calibrate_samples=1500`. If that still improves perf without quality degradation, we can create a new profile `aggressive-int8-v2b` that uses a different calibration strategy. Note: fp8 is promising but quality regressions are model-specific; don't enable fp8 in prod canary until we have evals.

Sam (support): Did a quick rollback to `balanced-int8-v1` at 02:45Z. Monitoring shows partial recovery: p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.1s. Better but still higher than baseline.

Alex (eng-runtime): Ok partial recovery suggests mixed causes: some requests are still hitting slow codepaths (maybe old workers or in-flight requests on nodes with different kernel selection). Next steps: 1) ensure all workers fully rolled to balanced-int8-v1 image (check node labels + restart timestamps), 2) collect perf traces for slow requests across multiple nodes, 3) log `kvcache` hit/miss per-request + batch sizes.

Priya (eng-ml): For a robust fix we need: calibration re-run with prod-like corpus, run our evaluation harness (ROUGE/BLEU/embedding-sim) on a small prompt set to verify quality, and produce a performance report (latency distribution by kernel). I can own the calibration run if eng-runtime gives me access to the artifact store and the `quantize` job config.

Jing (customer-success): I've told the customer we rolled back and are doing a deeper investigation. They're okay with temporary fp16 if it stabilizes tails, but will ask about cost impact. Please keep me posted so I can give ETA. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary-deploy dsp-hosted-13b-42 -> rolled back to balanced-int8-v1 by sam at 2026-03-15T02:45:07Z :information_source:

Tara (eng-sre): Short repro checklist for support to capture next slow example: 1) collect `request_id` and wall time 2) include `X-Redwood-Worker` header from response 3) attach `server-runtime.log` slice +/- 5s and `perf_trace.txt` 4) paste `batch_size` and `queue_length` from the API metrics at the time.

Sam (support): Will gather and send to Alex+Priya. For immediate follow-up: I'll schedule calibration with Priya, run a canary with `aggressive-int8-v2b` only after perf+quality report. Thanks all. :pray:
